samples.summary: `upstreamErrorJson` discards the server's human-readable failure reason for all non-envelope bodies (the common Nest error shape), leaving only `HTTP <status>`
samples.evidence: `upstreamErrorJson` returns `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR', message:`HTTP ${res.status}`}}` for any body that is not the documented envelope. The backend does not have a global envelope exception filter (grep for ExceptionFilter under packages/backend/src returns nothing); real upload failures throw plain Nest exceptions — `packages/backend/src/file/file.service.ts:106` `new BadRequestException('File too large (max 25 MB)')` and `packages/backend/src/file/file.controller.ts:35` `new BadRequestException('No file uploaded')` — which serialize to `{message, error:'Bad Request', statusCode:400}`. Before this delta, `files upload`/`docs import`/`notes import`/`slides import` printed that body verbatim, so stderr carried the actual reason; now that reason is dropped entirely and the operator/agent sees only `HTTP 400`. A cheap fix is to fold a string `message`/`error` from the framework body into the synthesized envelope's `message` instead of throwing it away.

samples.summary: `files download` can emit `{code:'HTTP_ERROR', message:'HTTP 200'}` when the response succeeded but carried no bytes
samples.evidence: The guard is `if (!res.ok || !res.bytes)`, so it also fires on a successful response with a missing `bytes` field (BinaryResponse declares `bytes?: Uint8Array`, packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:47). In that branch `upstreamErrorJson(res)` interpolates `res.status`, producing the self-contradictory body `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 200"}}` — an error message naming a success status, with no indication that the real problem was an empty body. Previously the printed body was `res.data ?? {code:'HTTP_ERROR'}` with no misleading status. The ok-but-no-bytes case deserves its own code/message (e.g. EMPTY_RESPONSE).
